Hi Lukas — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs we captured
- Strict EU data residency for customer PII and derived artifacts; data cannot be routed or stored outside the EU.
- Low latency for EU users (primary region eu-west / eu-central).
- Evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for compliance and procurement.

How each deployment mode maps to your asks
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed in EU regions): fastest time-to-value; we can ensure EU-only processing and storage when you select an EU account/region. No cross-region routing by default if account is configured for EU-only.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in our EU regions or colocated in customer cloud): gives predictable throughput and can be isolated to EU regions; good middle ground for procurement and performance.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over networking and data flow; meets the strictest compliance and procurement requirements but has longer lead time.

Open items / next steps
1) I will share our SOC 2 report, a deployment architecture diagram, and a draft pricing estimate for Dedicated vs Private (attached).
2) Marissa (SE) will follow up with capacity sizing and PoC timelines.
3) Confirm a 30-min follow-up next Friday 2026-09-17 10:00 CET to walk procurement + infra through options.

If you need anything before then (procurement POC requirements, specific region names), let me know and I’ll get it over.

Hi Lukas / Aditya — following up with more detail on the deployment tradeoffs and timelines so procurement and infra have concrete info.

1) Region availability (EU):
- Hosted & Dedicated: we currently run in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). We can guarantee data/process stays in-region for EU tenants.
- Private VPC: we support customer-managed VPC peering in AWS/GCP/Azure in EU regions; for on-prem we provide an air-gapped package and an ops runbook.

2) Cross-region routing and model pinning:
- Dedicated: can be provisioned and pinned to a single region (no cross-region fallback). Recommended for low-latency and predictable throughput.
- Hosted: EU-only tenants will not cross-route to non-EU infra; fallback behavior is configurable per-tenant.

3) Timeline & PoC:
- Dedicated PoC (reserved capacity in EU): ~4 weeks (procurement + infra prep + validation).
- Private VPC (customer-managed): ~6–8 weeks depending on networking approvals; on-prem air-gapped ~10–12 weeks.

4) Notes on performance/architecture:
- We recommend quantized model variants for Dedicated to hit your latency targets at lower cost; we’ll supply model profiles and token-cost estimates.
- KV/prefix cache config can be tuned to keep per-request latency low while benefiting from batching for throughput.

I’ve attached a short PDF summarizing Dedicated options (dedicated-options.pdf). Happy to present a 30‑minute technical session to FinBank infra during the Friday call.

Thanks,
